body: Independent read-only review (a fresh general-purpose subagent given the diff 5992fac5...a666ac42, the task file, the Bot row and the re-plan, not the worker's conclusions): red confirmed on 3887df89 (the old code() reported the quoted lines 6 and 7 and missed 2 to 5), green at the head (five tests, both checkout sweeps); ruff format and check clean; numstat 62 added and 32 removed in the one test file, nothing outside; a 49-fixture old-versus-new harness: the quoted pipe, semicolon, ampersand, the escaped quote with a quoted hash and an adjacent-span 'it'"|"'s' are now refused and echo "a\" # /tmp" is tmp-refused, while quoted data such as diff 'x <(a)' b and echo "diff" <(a) is no longer refused; a /usr/bin/grep of the tracked roots finds zero lines of the two newly accepted shapes; the predicate move is the four byte-identical closures with the signature the mechanism forces, judged within 'no other change'. Verdict: correct. This is local process evidence, not the task-level audit or reviewer authentication.

Three P3 notes. Fixed in 0b72f4c8: the scan() docstring said the continuation is read from the syntax view while logical_lines() reads the code view (the right choice: a backslash before the newline continues inside double quotes too, where the syntax view is blanked); the docstring now says so. Declared, not changed (outside D-S1-395's three quote kinds; zero tracked lines use either): ANSI-C quoting $'a\'b' is read as a plain single-quoted span, so the escaped quote closes it and the rest of the line is blanked (echo $'a\'b' | diff <(a) <(b) is accepted); a quoted command word ('diff' <(a) <(b)) is blanked and accepted although bash runs diff. Noted as unchanged behaviour: an unclosed quote suppresses the comment cut to the end of the line; a naive quote toggle leaves the inner operator of "$(cmd "x|y")" visible; echo a\ # /tmp is cut at the hash in both versions.
